# Intent recovery: can a fresh reader state what each unit must do
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #150, sha256:24bc678d9df0afb7ce409bfd4d15740acdef17b72da16de49a1ed0a62caf9746). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Ready
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** data (a pre-registered study)
- **Milestone:** Purpose: verifiability, preserved intent and reviewability
- **Source:** Steve's purpose-level ruling relayed by Dispatch, 2026-10-28 (VISION ruling 7: Phrase is not meant to beat C#; it solves the problems of AI-written code being unaccountable, unverifiable at the speed it is written, with intent vanishing with the prompt) and Decider D99 (Codex Yes, Grok Support-it). The head-to-head benchmark stays published as context and is not the success measure.
- **Depends on:** 134
- **Story:** As Steve, I want a fresh model, and later a human, to read a codebase in each form and state what each unit is supposed to do, including edge and failure cases, so that I can see whether intent survives the prompt.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given a design Decider written before any row, When it is read, Then it fixes the units, the sealed original intent statements, the scoring rubric (what counts as a correct statement of purpose, of each edge case and of each failure case), the readers and versions, the blinding (the reader sees one form per unit, the scorer does not know the form) and the Goodhart guard
  2. Given a codebase in each form (Phrase with its specs, plain C# with its tests and comments as the team normally writes them), When a fresh reader states each unit's intent, Then each row records form, unit, the statement's score per rubric item and the reader
  3. Given the rows, When summarized, Then recovery per form and per item kind (purpose, edge, failure) is shown with its uncertainty and no verdict beyond the pre-registered sentence

## Context

- Goodhart guard (D99): the design Decider fixes before any row the sample, the planted cases or mutants, the scoring rubric, timing and blinding or randomization, the model and reviewer versions and matched proof levels; mutant operators and review cases are frozen and sealed from the authors who tune Phrase; speed is reported with accuracy; the success sentence is written first.
- A human reader round is a later card; this one uses models.
